subsystems.name: Neural front end
subsystems.role: senses the tiny voltages from neurons and digitises them without leaking information.

subsystems.name: Wireless telemetry link
subsystems.role: carries decoded commands and raw neural data between implant and external device.

subsystems.name: On-device decoder
subsystems.role: turns neural activity into intent before it leaves the body.

subsystems.name: Identity and authentication layer
subsystems.role: confirms that the person using the interface is the enrolled user.

subsystems.name: Cryptographic core
subsystems.role: generates, stores and rotates keys, including quantum-resistant ones.
parts: post-quantum key exchange and signature algorithms

subsystems.name: Lifecycle management
subsystems.role: lets the device be updated, audited and shut down safely over its decade-long life.

subsystems.name: Privacy and audit
subsystems.role: governs neural data, which can reveal intent, mood and health.

buildSteps.title: Write the threat model
buildSteps.detail: List what an attacker could do: eavesdrop on the radio link, replay a recorded signal, impersonate a user, tamper with firmware or coerce the implant into unsafe stimulation.

buildSteps.title: Create a hardware root of trust
buildSteps.detail: A small secure element generates keys inside the chip and never exports them; it is the anchor for every other check.

buildSteps.title: Enrol the user
buildSteps.detail: Record a stable baseline of the person's own neural signatures and store it as a protected template, not raw recordings, so it cannot be replayed if stolen.

buildSteps.title: Secure the radio link
buildSteps.detail: Pair the implant and external device with authenticated key exchange, rotate session keys, and add sequence numbers so an old transmission cannot be replayed.

buildSteps.title: Push decoding on-device
buildSteps.detail: Run the decoder inside the implant or headset so raw neural data is not streamed continuously; only the minimum necessary result leaves the device.

buildSteps.title: Protect updates and revocation
buildSteps.detail: Firmware is signed by the manufacturer and verified before flashing; each device holds a revocable identity so a lost or compromised unit can be shut out.

buildSteps.title: Add anomaly detection
buildSteps.detail: Monitor the neural stream and the radio traffic for patterns that look like tampering, electrode drift or an unusual stimulation command, and fail safe rather than fail open.

buildSteps.title: Test adversarially
buildSteps.detail: Red teams attempt side-channel, replay, impersonation and stimulation attacks on bench hardware before any human trial.

prerequisites.why: some electrode arrays are in clinical trials and consumer headsets are sold, but the security architecture is an afterthought rather than a design input.
implanted electronics have tight power and heat budgets; cryptography must fit inside a few milliwatts.
quantum-resistant standards were published in 2024, but their footprint on tiny, battery-limited medical devices is still being worked out.
a usable identifier must stay recognisable across days, electrode drift and changing mental state — this is not yet demonstrated.
without clear legal treatment of brain data, engineers lack a defined standard for consent, retention and breach reporting.

pathway.milestone: academic neurosecurity research showing that consumer EEG and implanted links can be eavesdropped or manipulated
pathway.unlocks: a shared vocabulary of threats and a case for designing security in from the start.

pathway.milestone: reference security architectures for medical BCIs: hardware root of trust, authenticated pairing, signed updates
pathway.unlocks: regulators and manufacturers can test against something concrete rather than ad hoc.

pathway.milestone: demonstrated neural biometrics and privacy-preserving on-device decoding
pathway.unlocks: interfaces that can be used in public or clinical settings without streaming a person's brain activity to the cloud.

pathway.milestone: certification schemes and standards for neural devices, covering key management and lifetime support
pathway.unlocks: implanted interfaces that can be trusted for decades and safely decommissioned at end of life.
